this is a cool idea for alot of things. but would likely require a pretty significant change to the way vrchat handles position data and things like it. i could see it becoming its own update with udon. like a udon combat update so you can detect what part of the body you hit to. like just a whole combat update for udon in general would be nice. i think theres some jank ways to do lag compensation in udon but there not the most performant. a native solution would be nicer

the other option is using udon to register hits on the senders side not the receivers. like i said a little jank but would work pretty well and as long you properly _ your events is should be mostly safe from people exploiting it.

There's no way VRChat can implement this request unless you specify what exactly you'd like to be changed.
"Lag compensation" is such a broad term. And I think there's a *lot* of misinformation in this thread... 😫
For example, if I stab someone in Murder... What should happen? How should VRChat compensate for lag? What role should the master play? What tools are world creators missing? Why can't we compensate for lag ourselves?
As a world creator, I try to give the local user the benefit of the doubt, unless it's a competitive game. And it's been working OK so far. I'd like to have more control on how remote player movement is interpolated... Would you describe that as 'lag compensation'? Or should that be a different Canny?

Would be nice to see a game networking/instance option that sacrifices IK sync or uses a different networking system for absolutely lowest possible latency for player position, network events and variables.

author.name: Scout - VRChat Head of Quality Assurance

comments.value: It is clear that the games worked until there was an update. Since then we have had to be annoyed with this extreme delay! Regardless of whether you're playing shooter or catch, the delay has been extremely frustrating ever since. When playing catch, you get caught even if the other person is still 7 meters away. With the shooter, you will be shot down even if you have been in cover for 5 seconds. It's no fun anymore.
As an Avatar-PVP world creator, I can't help but say this was needed since the start.

details: Currently, any game world that uses the build in vrchat combat and ragdoll system has horrible latency issues since bullet hits are registered client side. I'm no programmer, but a server-side lag compensation system with regards to player position could make these game worlds feel much more responsive and less frustrating for the players.
title: Lag Compensation for PVP-based game worlds.
